questions.stem: What does 「かんきょう」 mean?
options: nature reserve
environment
economy
climate
questions.explanation: 「かんきょう」 is the environment: 「かんきょうをまもる」 is to protect the environment. The economy is 「けいざい」 and climate 「きこう」.

questions.stem: How do you say 'environment' in Japanese?
options: かんきょう
かんこう
けいざい
けんこう
questions.explanation: 「かんきょう」 is the environment. 「かんこう」, sightseeing, differs only in its middle sound, so read 「きょ」 carefully; 「けいざい」 is the economy and 「けんこう」 health.

questions.stem: What does 「ごみを分ける」 mean?
options: to burn rubbish
to sort rubbish
to reduce rubbish
to pick up rubbish
questions.explanation: 「分ける」 is to divide or separate, so rubbish is sorted by type before it goes out. Reducing it is 「へらす」, picking it up 「ひろう」 and burning it 「もやす」.

questions.stem: On a Japanese rubbish calendar, what is 「もえるごみ」?
options: Cans and glass bottles
Large items such as furniture
Burnable rubbish
Plastic bottles
questions.explanation: 「もえる」 is to burn, so 「もえるごみ」 goes to the incinerator. Plastic bottles are 「ペットボトル」, and large items are 「そだいごみ」, which usually need booking.

questions.stem: What does 「ちきゅうおんだんか」 mean?
options: global warming
air pollution
a water shortage
the loss of forests
questions.explanation: 「ちきゅう」 is the Earth and 「おんだんか」 is warming. Air pollution is 「たいきおせん」, and a water shortage 「水ぶそく」.

questions.stem: What does 「買い物に行く時は、エコバッグを持っていきます。」 mean?
options: I take a reusable bag when I go shopping.
I buy a reusable bag when I go shopping.
I bring a reusable bag home from the shops.
I lend my reusable bag to people who shop.
questions.explanation: 「持っていく」 is to take something with you as you go, and 「〜時は」 is 'when'. Bringing it back towards where you are now would be 「持ってくる」, and buying is 「買う」.

questions.stem: Read the notice: 「電気をむだにしないように、使わない時はけしましょう。」 What does it ask?
options: Avoid using electrical appliances at all if you can
Buy appliances that use less power when you replace them
Switch things off when not in use, so as not to waste power
Use electrical appliances only at night, when power is cheap
questions.explanation: 「〜ないように」 is 'so as not to', here 'so as not to waste electricity', and 「使わない時はけしましょう」 is 'let's turn them off when we're not using them'. Nothing is said about times of day or buying.

questions.stem: Read the notice: 「ごみは朝8時までに出してください。火曜日と金曜日はもえるごみ、水曜日はびんとかんです。」 When should cans go out?
options: Friday, after 8 am
Wednesday, after 8 am
Wednesday, by 8 am
Tuesday, by 8 am
questions.explanation: 「びんとかん」, bottles and cans, are collected 「水曜日」. 「8時までに」 means 'by 8 o'clock', a deadline, so after 8 am is too late. Tuesday and Friday are for burnable rubbish.

questions.stem: What does 「人口がへっています。」 mean?
options: The population is getting older.
The population is staying the same.
The population is falling.
The population is rising.
questions.explanation: 「人口」 (じんこう) is population, and 「へる」 is to decrease; increasing is 「ふえる」. Getting older would be 「こうれいかしています」.

questions.stem: How do you say 'to increase' in Japanese?
options: へる
かわる
のびる
ふえる
questions.explanation: 「ふえる」 is to increase in number: 「こうれいしゃがふえています」. 「へる」 is its opposite, 「かわる」 is to change, and 「のびる」 is to stretch or grow longer.

questions.stem: What does 「こうれいしゃ」 mean?
options: young people
high school students
office workers
elderly people
questions.explanation: 「こうれいしゃ」 are people of advanced age. Young people are 「わかもの」, high school students 「高校生」 and office workers 「会社いん」.

questions.stem: What does 「しょうしこうれいか」 describe?
options: A rising number of workers from overseas
A growing number of large families
People moving from cities to the country
Fewer births and an ageing population
questions.explanation: 「しょうしか」 is a falling birth rate, literally 'fewer children', and 「こうれいか」 is population ageing. Together they are a major topic of discussion in Japan.

questions.stem: What is a 「かくかぞく」?
options: A nuclear family of parents and children
An extended family of three generations
A family with only one parent at home
A family with a large number of children
questions.explanation: 「かくかぞく」 is a household of parents and their children only. Three generations under one roof, with grandparents, is 「さんせだい家族」, more common in the past.

questions.stem: Read: 「むかしは、そふぼとおやと子どもがいっしょに住む家が多かったです。今は、おやと子どもだけの家族がふえています。」 What change is described?
options: Families now have more children than they used to
Fewer children now live with their parents at all
More households now have only parents and children
More grandparents now live with their grandchildren
questions.explanation: 「むかしは」 is 'in the past' and 「今は」 'now'. Three generations together used to be common; now 「おやと子どもだけの家族」, parents-and-children-only families, are increasing.

questions.stem: What does 「ともばたらき」 mean?
options: working overtime
both parents working
working from home
working part-time
questions.explanation: 「とも」 is 'together' and 「はたらき」 is working, so 「ともばたらきの家族」 is a family where both parents have jobs. Working from home is 「テレワーク」 and overtime is 「ざんぎょう」.

questions.stem: What does 「かいご」 mean?
options: retirement from a full-time job
a pension paid to retired people
a medical check-up at a hospital
care of elderly or disabled people
questions.explanation: 「かいご」 is nursing care, often of elderly family members. A pension is 「ねんきん」, and retiring is 「たいしょく」.

questions.stem: Read: 「日本では、ひとりでくらすこうれいしゃがふえています。そのため、近所の人がときどきこえをかけるようにしている町もあります。」 What do some towns do?
options: Young people are asked to move in with elderly people
Elderly people visit local schools to talk to students
Neighbours check in on elderly people living alone
Elderly people who live alone are moved into hospitals
questions.explanation: 「こえをかける」 is to speak to someone, to say hello and see how they are. 「そのため」, 'for that reason', links it to the rise in elderly people living alone.

questions.stem: Read: 「父も母も働いているので、私は毎日弟のせわをしなければなりません。でも、そのおかげで弟とはとてもなかがいいです。」 How does the writer feel about looking after her brother?
options: Her parents look after him when she is busy
She does it only when her parents are away
It is a duty, but it has brought them close
It is a duty she wishes she could give up
questions.explanation: 「しなければなりません」 makes it an obligation, and 「でも、そのおかげで」, 'but thanks to that', turns to the good result: 「なかがいい」. Both parents work, so they are not home to do it.

questions.stem: What does 「けんさくする」 mean?
options: to download a file
to delete a message
to log in to a site
to search online
questions.explanation: 「けんさく」 is a search, as on a search engine: 「ネットでけんさくしました」. Deleting is 「さくじょ」, and download and log in are borrowed: 「ダウンロード」, 「ログイン」.

questions.stem: What does 「SNSにしゃしんをのせる」 mean?
options: to take a photo of a screen
to delete a photo from social media
to print a photo from social media
to post a photo on social media
questions.explanation: 「SNS」 is the usual Japanese word for social media, and 「のせる」 is to put something on, here to post it. Deleting would be 「けす」 or 「さくじょする」.

questions.stem: What does 「スマホを見ながら歩くのはあぶないです。」 mean?
options: Walking while looking at a phone is dangerous.
Looking at a phone after a walk is dangerous.
Walking without a phone with you is dangerous.
Walking to a shop to buy a phone is dangerous.
questions.explanation: Verb stem + 「ながら」 is doing two things at once, so 「見ながら歩く」 is walking while looking. 「〜のは」 turns the action into the topic, 'doing this is dangerous'.

questions.stem: What does 「ネットいぞん」 mean?
options: internet addiction
internet shopping
online bullying
an internet connection
questions.explanation: 「いぞん」 is dependence, so 「ネットいぞん」 is being unable to stop using the internet. Online bullying is 「ネットいじめ」, which looks similar.

questions.stem: What does 「こじんじょうほう」 mean?
options: a private message
a password
personal information
a personal opinion
questions.explanation: 「こじん」 is an individual and 「じょうほう」 is information, such as a name, address or phone number. An opinion is 「いけん」, and a password is 「パスワード」.

questions.stem: Read: 「SNSはべんりですが、知らない人に自分の住所や学校の名前を教えてはいけません。」 What is the warning?
options: Don't follow people whose names you don't know
Don't tell strangers your address or school name
Don't use social media while you are at school
Don't post photos of your friends without asking
questions.explanation: 「〜てはいけません」 forbids something, and what is forbidden is telling 「知らない人」, strangers, your 「住所」, address, or school name. The 「ですが」 after 「べんり」 sets up the warning.

questions.stem: Read: 「ニュースによると、来年から新しいごみのルールが始まるそうです。」 What does 「そうです」 show?
options: The writer thinks it looks likely to happen
The writer is sure it will happen
The writer plans to make it happen
The writer heard it from the news
questions.explanation: Plain form + 「そうです」 is hearsay, 'I hear that', and 「ニュースによると」 names the source. Verb stem + 「そうです」, as in 「雨がふりそうです」, means 'looks like', which is the trap.

questions.stem: What does 「メールがとどきました。」 mean?
options: An email has arrived.
I have sent an email.
I have deleted an email.
I wrote an email.
questions.explanation: 「とどく」 is to reach or arrive, and 「メール」 is its subject with 「が」. Sending is 「おくる」, and you would say 「メールをおくりました」 with 「を」.

questions.stem: What does 「インターネットでしらべてみます。」 mean?
options: I'll ask someone rather than look it up online.
I was asked to look it up on the internet.
I'll try looking it up on the internet.
I have already looked it up online.
questions.explanation: 「しらべる」 is to look up or investigate, and 「〜てみます」 is 'try doing and see'. Having already done it would be 「しらべました」.

questions.stem: An advertisement says 「今なら、二つ目はむりょう。」 What does it offer?
options: From today, everything is half price
Delivery is free for two weeks from now
The first two items are free from today
If you buy now, the second one is free
questions.explanation: 「今なら」 is 'if (you buy) now', a limited-time offer, and 「二つ目」 is 'the second one'. 「むりょう」 is free of charge; half price would be 「半がく」.

questions.stem: An advertisement ends 「お早めにどうぞ。」 What does it urge?
options: The shop now opens earlier than before
Breakfast is served early here
Come back later when the shop is quiet
Get in early so you don't miss out
questions.explanation: 「早め」 is 'on the early side', so 「お早めに」 urges customers to act soon, before the offer or stock runs out. It is about acting quickly, not about the morning.

questions.stem: What does 「きかんげんてい」 on a product mean?
options: Sold only online
Sold only in one region
For a limited time only
For members only
questions.explanation: 「きかん」 is a period of time and 「げんてい」 is limited, so the product is only sold for a while. Sold only in one region is 「ちいきげんてい」, the other common 「げんてい」.

questions.stem: Why might a Japanese advertisement for teenagers use plain forms such as 「やってみよう！」?
options: To show respect to older readers and parents
Because polite forms cannot be used in writing
Because the advertisement is for a formal event
To sound friendly and close to young readers
questions.explanation: The plain volitional 「やってみよう」, 'let's give it a go', is how friends talk, so it builds a friendly tone. An advertisement for adults would more often say 「やってみませんか」 or use 「です・ます」.

questions.stem: What does 「べんり」 mean?
options: convenient
expensive
dangerous
difficult
questions.explanation: 「べんり」 is convenient or handy: 「スマホはべんりです」. Its opposite is 「ふべん」, inconvenient. It is a な-adjective, so 「べんりなアプリ」.

questions.stem: What does 「ぎじゅつ」 mean?
options: an invention
a machine
technology
science
questions.explanation: 「ぎじゅつ」 is technology or technique: 「新しいぎじゅつ」. Science is 「かがく」, an invention 「はつめい」 and a machine 「きかい」.

questions.stem: What does 「ロボットが人のかわりに働いています。」 mean?
options: People are working to repair robots.
Robots are working in place of people.
People are working to change robots.
Robots and people are working side by side.
questions.explanation: Noun + 「のかわりに」 is 'instead of', so the robots do the work people used to do. 「かわり」 comes from 「かわる」, to take the place of, not from 「かえる」, to change.

questions.stem: What does 「この店では、スマホでお金がはらえます。」 mean?
options: You must pay with a phone at this shop.
You can't pay with a phone at this shop.
You can get cash with a phone at this shop.
You can pay with a phone at this shop.
questions.explanation: 「はらえます」 is the potential of 「はらう」, to pay, so it means 'can pay'. 'Must pay' would be 「はらわなければなりません」, and 'can't' 「はらえません」.

questions.stem: What does 「オンラインじゅぎょう」 mean?
options: online classes
online shopping
online games
online banking
questions.explanation: 「じゅぎょう」 is a class or lesson, so these are lessons held over the internet. Online shopping is 「ネットショッピング」 or 「ネットで買い物」.

questions.stem: Read: 「テクノロジーのおかげで生活はべんりになりました。しかし、家族と話す時間がへったと言う人もいます。」 What does the writer say?
options: Everyone agrees technology has only made life better
Families spend more time together thanks to phones
Life is easier, but some say family talk time has fallen
Life is harder, but families now talk more than before
questions.explanation: 「おかげで」 credits technology with a good result, and 「しかし」, 'however', brings in the other side. 「〜と言う人もいます」, 'some people say', shows it is one view, not everyone's.

questions.stem: Which word completes 「スマホの___、夜おそくまでねられません。」?
options: とおりに
せいで
おかげで
かわりに
questions.explanation: 「〜のせいで」 blames something for a bad result: because of the phone, I can't sleep until late. 「おかげで」 is for good results, 'thanks to', so it does not suit losing sleep.

questions.stem: Which sentence gives a balanced view, as in an essay?
options: 「SNSにはいい点もありますが、もんだい点もあると思います。」
「SNSはぜったいにだめだと思います。」
「SNSは一番べんりなものです。」
「SNSは毎日使います。」
questions.explanation: 「〜もありますが、〜もあります」 weighs good points against problems, which suits evaluative writing. 「ぜったいにだめ」 is one-sided, and the last two give no view of both sides.
